offers.name: Lenovo Legion Pro 5i 16" WQXGA 240Hz Gaming Laptop, Intel Core Ultra 7 251HX, GeForce RTX 5070 Ti 12GB GDDR7, 64GB RAM, 4TB SSD+1TB Dock Set, RGB Backlit, Win 11, Eclipse Black

reviews.quote: It's built well and clean looking, offers solid ergonomics, decent inputs, and a beautiful OLED display that you won't normally find in this segment.
strong raster performance from the RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU, excellent motion clarity from the 240Hz 2560×1600 OLED, and a cooling design that sustains clocks without resorting to gimmicks.
it focuses on nailing the fundamentals: strong performance, a fantastic display, sturdy build quality, and a keyboard that's genuinely comfortable to use.

professional.note: Pro scores are for the tested Ultra 9 275HX / RTX 5070 Ti / 32GB config (NBC collection 86.8%); this tier's ratings inferred per SHARED-legion-pro5.md deltas.

praises: OLED 240Hz panel at a sub-$4,500 sale price is the segment standout — inky blacks and motion clarity rare at this tier
RTX 5070 Ti at up to 140W TGP handles WQXGA max settings; Ultrabook Review notes the GPU is "properly tamed in this chassis"
Dual SODIMM + dual M.2 (Gen5-capable) — easy user upgrades to 64GB/4TB+, unlike soldered-RAM rivals
TrueStrike keyboard widely called genuinely comfortable for long gaming/work sessions
PD charging + Thunderbolt/USB4 make it usable for office duty despite the gaming skin
complaints: Some Gen 10 Legion 50-series units hit nvlddmkm TDR black-screen crashes during gaming (platform-wide Legion reports); a few needed RMA
Keyboard deck gets hot and fans audible in Performance mode under sustained load
Battery is weak — roughly 4h light use, ~1h gaming; the laptop is a desk machine
Speakers are modest and there are no rear ports; everything clusters on sides/back-low
Regular $7,069 CAD is inflated — only the deep Lenovo/BBY sale cadence makes the line competitive; some OLED units reported red/subpixel bleed

design_philosophy: Lenovo's 'mainstream affordable Legion Pro' bet: take the Pro 7 chassis language, keep the strong 140W-class GPU cooling and comfortable TrueStrike keyboard, and differentiate with an OLED panel rarely seen at this tier — while trimming premium extras (rear I/O, big speaker arrays). This 275HX/5070 Ti/32GB/2TB tier is the sweet-spot config the professional reviewers tested and recommend: standouts = OLED 240Hz + upgradeable RAM/storage; dealbreakers for some = battery life and sale-price-dependent value.
rating_notes: Inferred from anchor 80 per SHARED-legion-pro5.md: +0.5 productivity / +0.5 ai_ml (64GB), +0.4 creative_work (4TB), -0.4 (251HX). Top Pro 5i tier.
